Location: Remote (Global)

Type: Internship

Company: Yotta Labs

Apply: careers@yottalabs.ai

🧠 About Yotta Labs

Yotta Labs is building the next generation multi-silicon AI cloud and runtime platform to power the world’s most demanding AI workloads. We enable training and inference across NVIDIA GPUs, AMD GPUs, and AWS Trainium, helping AI companies achieve the best performance and economics across heterogeneous hardware. Our mission is to provide high-performance AI computing and Model API services, enabling AI companies, research labs, and enterprises to train, deploy and integrate cutting-edge models at scale.

🛠️ Role Overview

We are seeking a highly motivated Research Engineer Intern to work on Trainium, GPU kernels, and LLM systems optimization. Over a 12–16 week internship, you will own a well-scoped project at the intersection of AI Systems, Compiler and Runtime Optimization, Distributed Training & Inference, GPU/Accelerator Kernel Development, and Large Language Model Infrastructure — taking it from design to working, profiled code running on real hardware. Your work will ship to production or open source and directly impact the performance of AI applications deployed on our platform. Strong interns receive return offers for full-time roles.

🎯 Responsibilities

- Implement and optimize compute kernels for Attention, GEMM, MoE, and quantization on NVIDIA, AMD, or AWS Trainium.

- Build custom operators using CUDA, Triton, ROCm/HIP, or the Neuron SDK with PyTorch/XLA.

- Profile and improve inference performance in vLLM, SGLang, and our custom runtimes — kernel fusion, scheduling, KV-cache and memory optimizations.

- Build benchmarks, chase down performance regressions, and turn profiler traces into concrete speedups.

- Ship code upstream to open-source AI infrastructure projects, with tests and documentation.

✅ Qualifications

- Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field.

- Solid programming skills in Python and familiarity with C++.

- Understanding of GPU/accelerator architecture fundamentals (memory hierarchy, parallelism, occupancy) from coursework, research, or projects.

- Experience writing CUDA, Triton, ROCm/HIP, or Neuron kernels — class projects and personal projects count.

- Strong understanding of AI frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, Dynamo, LMCache), model architectures and profiling tools (e.g. Nsight, ROCm Profiler, or Neuron Profiler).

- Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work independently in a collaborative, remote environment.

🌟 Preferred Experience

- Contributions to open-source AI infra projects like vLLM, SGLang, PyTorch, or Triton.

- Familiarity with LLM inference internals — FlashAttention, PagedAttention, continuous batching, speculative decoding, MoE, or quantization.

- Experience with profiling tools (e.g. Nsight, ROCm Profiler, Neuron Profiler, or PyTorch Profiler) and performance debugging on real workloads.

- Publications in top-tier conferences like MLSys, OSDI, SOSP, NSDI, SC, HPCA, or ISCA

🌐 Why Join Yotta Labs?

- Be part of a visionary team aiming to redefine AI infrastructure and influence the future of multi-silicon AI computing.

- Work on frontier AI infrastructure problems with access to serious hardware — latest-generation NVIDIA GPUs, AMD accelerators, and AWS Trainium at scale.

- Get direct mentorship from engineers from leading institutions and tech companies.

- Competitive internship compensation, a flexible remote work environment, and a fast path to a full-time return offer for top performers.

📩 How to Apply

Interested candidates should apply directly or send their resume to careers@yottalabs.ai. Please include links to any relevant projects or contributions (GitHub, open-source PRs, course projects) — for internships, these matter more to us than a cover letter.

Dow Jones Internship Program is a 10-week summer experience designed to give students real exposure to how . Our interns work on meaningful projects alongside our teams, gaining hands-on skills that make an impact on the business.

You will work as part of a global team that is responsible for strategic, long-term market forecasts for the chemical industry. Acacia, now part of Cisco, creates intelligent optical transceivers using advanced photonic integration for global telecommunication networks. You will design and validate firmware components essential for the bring-up and testing of our ultra-high data rate electro-optical modules. Working in our hardware organization, you will develop the infrastructure code needed to ensure our sub-systems function reliably. This role offers you the opportunity to solve complex engineering challenges while collaborating with cross-functional manufacturing and software teams to power the future of connectivity.

In this role, you will:

- Design and validate firmware for the bring-up of electro-optical modules.
- Develop and test infrastructure code for product evaluation sub-systems.
- Collaborate with hardware and software teams to integrate system components.
- Troubleshoot technical issues to ensure product stability and performance.

-An undergraduate degree program (Associate's or Bachelor's) with 2 years of work experience; or

-A Master’s degree program with 0 years of work experience.

-Expected to continue enrollment in degree program following completion of the internship.

- Working knowledge of RTOS, microcontrollers, or common embedded CPU architectures.
- Experience implementing low-level device drivers such as I2C, SPI, or UART protocols.
- Familiarity with FPGA/CPLD initialization and hardware/software bring-up processes.
- Exposure to Linux-based system programming or network programming using TCP/UDP/Sockets.

We work as a team, collaborating with empathy to make really big things happen on a global scale. Because our solutions are everywhere, our impact is everywhere.

We are Cisco, and our power starts with you.

The 2027 Summer Internship Program will run from May 17, 2027, through August 6, 2027. Candidates must be available to start on May 17 and participate through the duration of the program.

Who Are We?

The Toro Company (TTC) has delivered market-leading, innovative products and outstanding customer care for more than 100 years. With over 11,000 employees worldwide, TTC is headquartered in Bloomington, Minnesota, USA.

Our company designs and manufactures turf maintenance equipment; turf irrigation systems; landscape and lighting products; snow and ice management solutions; agricultural irrigation systems; rental, specialty and underground construction equipment; and residential turf and snow equipment. We market and sell TTC products worldwide through a network of distributors, dealers, mass retailers, hardware retailers, equipment rental center and home centers—as well as online direct to end users.

What Will You Do?

As an Embedded Software Engineering Intern, you'll have the opportunity to design cutting-edge embedded software applications for Toro equipment. Whether you're working independently or collaborating with a multi-disciplinary team, you'll gain hands-on experience in real-world projects that push the boundaries of technology. Key responsibilities include:

- Dive into the development, debugging, and enhancement of embedded firmware for electrification and autonomous projects.

- Be part of the team that investigates, defines, and specifies innovative new products.

- Collaborate with engineering team members to design and implement high-quality electronics and firmware solutions that meet cutting-edge product requirements.

- Play a key role in resolving integration challenges that involve multiple electronics, software applications, and developers.

- Work closely with electronic, system, and software design engineers to help optimize overall product performance.

- Get hands-on experience in the validation and testing of electronics and embedded software.

- Assist software engineers in defining interfaces and optimizing hardware/software performance.

- Thoroughly test and evaluate embedded software to ensure top-notch quality and functionality.

- Contribute to the creation of detailed hardware and firmware design and validation documentation.

What Do You Need?

To be considered for this role, an individual should meet the following minimal requirements:

- Currently a Junior or Senior student pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechanical Engineering or a related engineering field (required) with interest in embedded systems.

- Familiar with developing embedded firmware for 8/16/32-bit microcontrollers in C/C++.

- Experience with real-time operating systems (RTOS) is a plus.

- Knowledge of desktop application development in C++/C# is preferred.

- Familiar with common communication protocols such as SPI, I2C, RS232, and CAN.

- Strong understanding of the relationship between hardware and software, with the ability to design systems that integrate both technologies efficiently.

- Excellent oral and written communication skills.

- Thrives in a team environment.

- Results-driven, action-oriented, and full of positive energy.

- Strong problem-solving and resolution skills.

- High degree of integrity and commitment to achieving results.

- Independently self-motivated and have interpersonal skills to build relationships and collaborate within a team having a variety of cross-functional product responsibility.

What Can We Give You?

At The Toro Company, we are always working to make sure our interns know just how valued they are. In addition to a competitive pay- The Toro Company offers interns a variety of perks, including:

- Dress for your day – We know you're more productive when you're comfortable, which is why TTC employees are encouraged to take advantage of our casual, corporate environment.

- Volunteerism – The Toro Company is proud to provide interns 8 hours of paid time to volunteer in the community.

- Summer Hours *Based on Location* – Enjoy a flexible schedule during the summer! By working a little more during the first few days of the week, TTC employees at certain locations are able to start their weekends early and leave by noon on Friday.

- Competitive Pay – Competitive compensation with an anticipated hourly rate of $22–$28. Actual rates may vary based on factors such as academic standing, business function, and other relevant considerations.

Overview

SRI's Integrated Systems and Solutions (InSYS) division designs and develops leading-edge R&D technology that support demanding market needs. Located in Princeton, NJ, InSyS maintains a state-of-the-art products portfolio that includes real-time video processors, integrated video and sensor exploitation solutions, and instrumented training systems for government and commercial sectors.

InSyS's Center for Advanced Imaging Embedded Software Team is seeking innovative, highly motivated individuals to join us in the development of software. The ideal candidate would join a multidisciplinary group dedicated to the development of custom image sensor devices, modules, and systems for numerous commercial, spacecraft, and government applications - more specifically, development of high-speed cameras for applications such as low light imaging, space base imagers, and LiDAR cameras.

This position will work from our office in Princeton, NJ.

Responsibilities

- Designing and implementing software of embedded devices and systems

- Designing, developing, coding, testing, and debugging system software

- Analyzing and enhancing efficiency, stability, and scalability of system resources

Qualifications

- Current Drexel University student majoring in Computer Science, Electrical/Computer/Software Engineering

- Due to government contract requirements candidates must be a US Citizen

- Programming experience in C/C++ or Python.

- Experience in embedded system, i.e., microcontroller, ARM

- Familiarity with software configuration management tools, IDE, bug tracking and code revision tools (GitLab or Git)

Desired qualifications:

- Experience with I2C, SPI, or UART

- Analysis and laboratory automation experience, including development experience with automation and analysis tools such as Python.
